_notice: DEMO FIXTURE. Labelled addresses are real (research/data label sets); suspect/hop addresses, tx hashes, amounts and confidences are synthetic placeholders for UI development. Not evidence.

rows.text: Automatically analyze suspect cryptocurrency wallet addresses reported during investigations on the Sahyog Platform.
rows.what: An intake API takes a complaint with its wallets, opens one case per wallet and traces each without anyone touching the tool; the result is handed back through the gateway.
rows.gap: SAHYOG's real interface is not public. This is our side of a contract, demonstrated with a simulator; nothing has been connected to the portal.

rows.text: Automatically trace blockchain transaction paths to identify: nearest centralized exchange, custodial wallet service, or VASP receiving direct deposits from the suspect wallet.
rows.what: A wallet's money is followed hop by hop to the nearest labelled exchange, custodial wallet or swap service, in both directions. The exchange is named only when the label evidence holds; otherwise the case says the evidence is insufficient.

rows.text: Map blockchain of deposit addresses and transaction flows across multiple blockchain networks such as: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BNB Chain, Solana, Polygon, and other major chains.
rows.what: Wallets are traced on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BNB Chain, Solana and Polygon, and on Arbitrum, Base and Optimism.

rows.text: Support identification of: exchange clusters, hot wallets, deposit wallets, mixers/tumblers, DeFi bridges, and cross-chain swap services.
rows.what: Labels carry the owner and the kind of wallet (hot, cold, deposit, reserve); Bitcoin addresses are clustered by co-spending; Tron deposit addresses are derived from sweeps and scored by a measured model; mixers, bridges and swap services are recognised from labels, and a CoinJoin from the shape of the transaction.

rows.text: Integrate Sahyog with blockchain intelligence APIs and graph analytics engines.
rows.what: The tracing and attribution engine is behind a documented HTTP API with a contract for both directions: complaints in, results and requests out, replies in.
rows.gap: The contract is our proposal. The real portal has not been connected, because its interface is not public.

rows.text: Provide automated tagging and confidence scoring for suspected VASPs.
rows.what: Each named exchange carries a calibrated confidence with an interval, kept apart from how near it is; the measurements behind it are on the model page.

rows.text: Generate investigation-ready reports for LEAs.
rows.what: Every finished case has an A4 case file (PDF): the result, where the funds went, the flow diagram, each exchange with its evidence and transaction hashes, the flags, the risk indicators, the limits, and a provenance receipt that can be verified.

rows.text: Assist investigators in automatically routing lawful disclosure or freezing requests to the correct VASP through the SAHYOG Portal.
rows.what: Wallets are grouped under the exchange they route to; one request per exchange is drafted with its legal basis, approved by the officer, handed to the gateway, and the exchange's reply is tracked to 'freeze confirmed'.
rows.gap: The gateway writes to a local outbox. Nothing is sent to the real portal or to an exchange.

rows.text: visualization of fund movement
rows.what: The Hop Rail, the fund-flow graph with a replay, the timeline and the 'where the funds went' bar on every case. The graph draws the wallet's own money only, and says so in the trace's own counts: how many transfers it saw, how many it followed, and why each other wallet was not followed. The rest of what it read can be switched on as greyed context, for one wallet or for all, without changing the answer. Many small payers of one wallet are drawn as one group that opens in place. An optional 3D view shows the same picture turned.

rows.text: cross-chain transaction mapping
rows.what: A deposit into the Across bridge is matched to its payout by the bridge's own public index, the amount is read from the payout transaction on the destination chain, and the trace goes on from the recipient there with the same rules; the crossing counts as a hop and its cost as a fee. The recorded wallet is followed from Ethereum onto Base. A swap service on the path is named as a VASP and its request asks for the payout chain, address and transaction.
rows.gap: Only Across deposits are matched. Stargate / LayerZero, Wormhole, Hop and the rollups' own bridges are recognised and flagged, and the trail ends there with the transaction to follow by hand. A payout in another asset than the deposit (a stablecoin paid out as ETH) is named but not followed. A swap service's payout cannot be matched on-chain at all: it is asked for.

rows.text: risk scoring
rows.what: A score from 0 to 100 built from named red-flag indicators, each with its points and the transactions behind it. It is an indicator score, not a probability. Checked on 8 Oct 2026 on 65 wallets public sources list as illicit and 70 with a documented ordinary purpose, each with its own label hidden: 14 of 65 and 2 of 70 scored High or above, all 14 through a link to another listed address; none of the five pattern rules fired more often on the listed wallets. The points were not fitted to these wallets.

rows.text: identification of laundering typologies
rows.what: Peel chains, fan-out, fan-in, forwarding within minutes, round amounts, bridge hops and CoinJoin shapes are flagged, each with the wallet, the figures and the transaction hashes. Checked on 8 Oct 2026 on 65 listed and 70 ordinary real wallets: each of the five pattern rules fired on ordinary wallets as often as on listed ones (peel chain 3 of 65 against 3 of 70, fan-out 8 against 15, fan-in 20 against 26, forwarding within minutes 13 against 21, round amounts 4 against 5), so a flag describes how money moved and is not by itself a sign of crime.

rows.text: alerting for high-risk wallets linked to ransomware, darknet, terrorism financing, or fraud ecosystems
rows.what: Labels carry threat tags from cited public sources (the OFAC SDN list, Ransomwhere, GraphSense TagPacks, scam lists): ransomware, darknet market, terrorism financing, fraud. A case is screened when it is opened, a link to a tagged address is an alert that names the threat and the source, and a watched wallet raises a change on a new link or a higher risk class. A wallet none of those sources lists raises nothing: the alert is only as wide as the lists, and they are uneven by chain (the Tron tags are terrorism financing and sanctions only; the ransomware and darknet tags are Bitcoin; fraud is mostly Ethereum).

rows.text: Automated identification of nearest VASP/exchange linked to unknown wallets.
rows.what: Paste a wallet and the nearest exchange comes back with its proximity and its confidence, or 'insufficient evidence' with what would change that.

rows.text: API-driven blockchain tracing and attribution support.
rows.what: Everything the interface does goes through the HTTP API (docs/api_contract.md, docs/openapi.json): open a case, read the result, the case file, the receipt.

rows.text: Multi-chain transaction analysis and visualization.
rows.what: Wallets are traced on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, BNB Chain, Solana and Polygon, and on Arbitrum, Base and Optimism.

rows.text: Real-time generation of investigative intelligence.
rows.what: A trace starts the moment a wallet is submitted and the case page shows what it has read so far. Measured on 5 Oct 2026: a complaint with the 12 recorded wallets, on six chains, went from intake to 12 results in 6.3 seconds (four runs, all between 6.3 and 6.4; artifacts/intake_timing.json).
rows.gap: That figure replays recorded chain responses with no network. A live trace also waits on the public chain APIs and their rate limits, which was not timed. Nothing watches a chain continuously: a watched wallet is checked when the officer asks.

rows.text: Risk classification of wallets and transaction flows.
rows.what: Every wallet and every case has a class (Low, Medium, High, Severe) with its reasons, and every traced transfer is classified by the indicators on it.

rows.text: Dashboard for LEAs with case-based analytics and reporting.
rows.what: Counts of cases by outcome, by chain and by risk class, the exchanges reached, requests awaiting reply and recent alerts, each counted from stored records and linked to the list behind it.

rows.text: Scalable architecture capable of handling large-volume blockchain transaction analysis.
rows.what: A batch of up to 2,000 wallets is uploaded, queued in a table that survives a restart, and traced by a pool of worker processes that share one response cache and one rate limit per provider. The officer can raise a trace's budget from 40 to 2,000 wallets. Measured on one machine: 410 cases a minute with one worker, 901 with four (artifacts/scale/metrics.json).
rows.gap: Measured on one laptop with chain responses replayed from a cache: live throughput, which the providers' rate limits bound, was not measured. More than four workers gave no gain there. The case store is a single file with one writing process, and nothing was run on more than one machine (docs/scaling.md).

rows.text: reduce investigation time
rows.what: A wallet is traced, attributed and written up as a case file and a draft request without manual chain analysis.
rows.gap: The time the tool takes is measured. The time the same work takes by hand has not been measured, so no saving is claimed.

rows.text: improve asset freezing efficiency
rows.what: A freeze can be asked for in the request (section 106 BNSS is added to the legal basis) and the request is tracked until the exchange confirms the freeze.
rows.gap: No request has gone to a real exchange, so no freeze has been made or timed.

rows.text: enhance attribution capabilities
rows.what: Attribution is measured, not asserted, on six chains beside a naive baseline: 761 real wallets that paid a labelled exchange were traced with the labels one hop away hidden (Tron 280, Ethereum 213, Bitcoin 96, BNB Chain 84, Polygon 74, Solana 14). The share named wrongly is on the model page for each chain (Tron 15 of 155, Ethereum 22 of 69, Bitcoin 2 of 28, BNB Chain 0 of 19, Polygon 0 of 11, Solana 0 of 3), with the deposit-address model's calibration error and coverage.

rows.text: strengthen cross-border cybercrime investigations involving VDAs
rows.what: Foreign exchanges are named and requests are routed to them with their legal name, jurisdiction and law-enforcement channel where a source for these was found.
rows.gap: The jurisdiction map is not built: no cited jurisdiction was found for the exchanges the recorded cases reach.

source: Smart India Hackathon problem statement 26182 (Ministry of Home Affairs, I4C), quoted word for word.
